items.title: Downloaded weights are loaded with an unguarded torch.load fallback (possible pickle code execution)

findings.title: Downloaded weights are loaded with an unguarded torch.load fallback (possible pickle code execution)
findings.evidence:
try:
        state = torch.load(path, map_location=device, weights_only=True)
    except TypeError:  # torch < 1.13
        state = torch.load(path, map_location=device)
findings.explanation: The common path is safe, but if unpickling with weights_only=True raises TypeError (torch older than 1.13, and any TypeError raised inside the unpickler), the same file is re-loaded as a full pickle through the second call. The files come from a network download (see next finding), so a modified .pth could run arbitrary Python in the Slicer process on such setups.
findings.suggestion: Remove the fallback and report a clear error asking the user to install PyTorch through the PyTorch extension, or at minimum only fall back after verifying the file against a pinned SHA-256.

findings.title: torch.load fallback triggers on any TypeError
findings.evidence:
try:
        state = torch.load(path, map_location=device, weights_only=True)
    except TypeError:  # torch < 1.13
        state = torch.load(path, map_location=device)
findings.explanation: _load wraps torch.load(weights_only=True) in a bare except TypeError and then calls torch.load without weights_only, which unpickles arbitrary objects. The intent is only for torch<1.13, but any TypeError raised inside the safe path would silently fall back to the unsafe load.
findings.suggestion: Check torch.__version__ (or inspect the signature) before choosing the call, and do not fall back to the unrestricted pickle load for any other exception.

items.title: License of the downloaded model weights is not stated

findings.title: License of the downloaded model weights is not stated
findings.evidence:
MIT License

Copyright (c) 2026 Burak Demir
findings.explanation: The extension's MIT license covers only the wrapper code. The ~140 MB weights are fetched from a different repository (4burakfe/DMSAAI) and the files reviewed do not state their terms. Users and redistributors cannot tell whether the weights may be used or redistributed, including for commercial use.
findings.suggestion: Confirm and state the license of the weights (in the DMSAAI repo or README), and note any non-commercial terms, since the extension downloads them on demand.

items.title: Model weights downloaded from a moving branch without integrity check

findings.title: Model weights downloaded from a moving branch without integrity check
findings.evidence: WEIGHTS_BASE_URL = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/4burakfe/DMSAAI/main/"
findings.explanation: download_weights() fetches each .pth from `raw.githubusercontent.com/4burakfe/DMSAAI/main/` (line 11, urlretrieve at line 192) with no expected hash and no pinned commit/tag. Whatever the `main` branch contains at download time is deserialized by torch (see previous finding), so content changes upstream silently propagate to users' machines; it also makes results non-reproducible between users.
findings.suggestion: Pin the download URLs to a specific commit (or release asset) and verify a published SHA-256 per file before use; state the hash list in the README so the provenance is auditable.

items.title: DICOM plugin switches module and replaces the layout without asking

findings.title: DICOM plugin switches module and replaces the layout without asking
findings.explanation: Loading any DMSA series in the DICOM module silently takes the user out of the DICOM module, and DMSAAILogic.showLayout() then replaces the current layout with the fixed 2x3 layout (DMSAAI.py:1052-1062). The opt-out key `DMSAAI/SwitchToModuleAfterDICOMLoad` is documented in the README but has no UI in the module, so a user must edit QSettings by hand.
findings.suggestion: Default the switch to off or expose a checkbox in the module's Advanced section; if the switch is kept, do not force the layout change on module entry.

items.title: Downloaded model weights are not integrity-checked

findings.title: Downloaded model weights are not integrity-checked
findings.evidence:
urllib.request.urlretrieve(WEIGHTS_BASE_URL + name, tmp)
        os.replace(tmp, target)
findings.explanation: download_weights fetches each .pth file from raw.githubusercontent.com with urllib.request.urlretrieve and no checksum or signature check, then loads it with torch.load. A compromised upstream repo or a network MITM would deliver arbitrary weights. The weights_only=True load limits code execution from pickle, but tampered weights could still change clinical outputs silently. Download is gated by user confirmation.
findings.suggestion: Pin SHA-256 hashes for each weight file and verify before os.replace; state the source commit of the weights in the docs.

items.title: Inference runs on the GUI thread and log() pumps the event loop

findings.title: Inference runs on the GUI thread and log() pumps the event loop
findings.explanation: segment()/classify() call the networks synchronously from the button handler (no thread, no progress bar), so Slicer is frozen during CPU inference of up to 7 networks and looks hung. Additionally log() calls `slicer.app.processEvents()` for every message (DMSAAI.py:319-323), which re-enters the event loop from within a slot and can let the user click buttons while preprocessed state is half-updated.
findings.suggestion: Run the analysis in a slicer.util.ProgressDialog worker (or disable/enable the buttons around a guarded event-process) and drop processEvents from log().

items.title: Module test does not reset the scene before the third test

findings.title: Module test does not reset the scene before the third test
findings.evidence:
def runTest(self):
        self.setUp()
        self.test_PlanarGeometry()
        self.setUp()
        self.test_QuantificationOnSyntheticImage()
        self.test_AnalysisSettings()
findings.explanation: test_AnalysisSettings runs on the scene left over from the quantification test, and it writes to the user's real Qt settings (settings.save_analysis_settings), restoring only the values it captured. If the test is interrupted between save and restore, the user's saved preferences are replaced by the test's values.
findings.suggestion: Call setUp() before every test and back up/restore the full QSettings group (or use a temporary settings scope).

items.title: No model provenance, validation or bundled sample data for an AI diagnostic-adjacent tool

findings.title: No model provenance, validation or bundled sample data for an AI diagnostic-adjacent tool
findings.evidence:
3. The model weights (about 140 MB) are downloaded from the DMSAAI repository on first use into Slicer's cache
   folder, after you confirm the download. You can point *Advanced → Model weights* at an existing DMSAAI folder
   instead.
findings.explanation: The README explains installation and usage but gives no training cohort, validation metrics, failure modes or reference publication for the segmentation and classification networks, and the tests require an external DMSAAI checkout (Testing/test_pipeline.py:28-29) instead of shipping a small anonymised sample study. Users cannot judge the reliability of the printed findings such as "Probable Abnormal Cortical Uptake".
findings.suggestion: Add a short model-provenance section (training data, reported accuracy, limitations) and ship or cite a small de-identified sample study.

items.title: No stated terms for the downloaded model weights and bundled colour maps

findings.title: No stated terms for the downloaded model weights and bundled colour maps
findings.evidence: WEIGHTS_BASE_URL = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/4burakfe/DMSAAI/main/"
findings.explanation: The extension code is MIT, but about 140 MB of .pth weights are fetched at runtime from the author's DMSAAI repository and seven colour-map CSVs are bundled (DMSAAI/Resources/ColorMaps) whose origin is undocumented. I could not verify that the upstream repository grants permission to redistribute these artefacts, so distribution permission for the bundled/downloaded material is unconfirmed.
findings.suggestion: State the license of the weights and of the colour maps in the README (and confirm the upstream DMSAAI repository carries a compatible license).

items.title: README button name does not match the UI

findings.title: README button name does not match the UI
findings.evidence:
5. Click **Clinical Evaluation** for the cortical abnormality, normal kidney, afunctional kidney and horseshoe
   kidney models.
findings.explanation: The README says to click 'Clinical Evaluation', but the widget button is labeled 'AI-powered Evaluation'. Users following the docs will not find the button.
findings.suggestion: Use the actual label 'AI-powered Evaluation' in the README.

items.title: Screenshot URL points to a different repository name

findings.title: Icon and screenshot URLs point to different repositories
findings.evidence:
set(EXTENSION_ICONURL "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/4burakfe/SlicerDMSAAI/main/DMSAAI.png")
set(EXTENSION_SCREENSHOTURLS "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/4burakfe/DMSAAI/main/scr.jpg")
findings.explanation: The icon is served from the extension repository while the screenshot is served from the separate stand-alone app repository on a moving `main` branch; a change or deletion there breaks the catalog listing silently. I could not fetch the URLs to confirm they resolve.
findings.suggestion: Serve both from the extension repository (scr.jpg is already committed there) and, if possible, pin to a commit or release asset.

findings.title: Screenshot URL points to a different repository name
findings.evidence:
set(EXTENSION_ICONURL "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/4burakfe/SlicerDMSAAI/main/DMSAAI.png")
set(EXTENSION_SCREENSHOTURLS "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/4burakfe/DMSAAI/main/scr.jpg")
findings.explanation: The screenshot URL uses the repo name DMSAAI while the source repo is SlicerDMSAAI; the icon URL uses SlicerDMSAAI. If scr.jpg is not present in the DMSAAI repo, the Extensions Manager screenshot will be broken. scr.jpg is also committed in this repo.
findings.suggestion: Point EXTENSION_SCREENSHOTURLS at the SlicerDMSAAI repo (main/scr.jpg), which contains the file.

items.title: monai/einops installed into Slicer's Python unpinned and with dependency resolution enabled

findings.title: monai/einops installed into Slicer's Python unpinned and with dependency resolution enabled
findings.evidence:
for requirement in missing:
            self.log(f"Installing {requirement}...")
            slicer.util.pip_install(requirement)
        importlib.invalidate_caches()
findings.explanation: `monai>=1.3` (REQUIREMENTS, DMSAAI.py:589-592) is an open-ended range, and pip_install resolves its transitive requirements into Slicer's shared environment, so a future MONAI release can pull different dependency versions (and its model API could change so the published weights no longer load). This affects all extensions sharing that Python once any user runs the install.
findings.suggestion: Use an upper bound (e.g. `monai>=1.3,<1.6`), consider `pip_install(..., no_deps=True)` where feasible, and record the tested MONAI version in the README.

items.title: Dependency installation can bypass the confirmation dialog

findings.title: Dependency installation can bypass the confirmation dialog
findings.explanation: The Advanced button installs packages without a second confirmation. This is an explicit user click on a button whose tooltip states it installs MONAI and einops, so it is informed consent in practice, but it is one click away from modifying Slicer's environment with no size/version information shown.
findings.suggestion: Show the exact requirements (and their resolved versions) in the confirmation dialog even for the button.

items.title: Model is reloaded from disk on every call

findings.title: Model is reloaded from disk on every call
findings.explanation: segment() and classify() rebuild the network and reload weights from disk on each click, including one DenseNet per kidney side and per class (up to 7 loads per evaluation). This is slow on CPU and adds memory churn, but it is not a correctness defect.
findings.suggestion: Cache loaded models keyed by path and device, and run long inference off the GUI thread with progress.

items.title: Patient name and ID are stored as node attributes and shown in the UI (local only)

findings.title: Patient name and ID are stored as node attributes and shown in the UI (local only)
findings.evidence:
if ds is not None:
        attributes[ATTR_PATIENT_ID] = str(getattr(ds, "PatientID", ""))
        attributes[ATTR_PATIENT_NAME] = str(getattr(ds, "PatientName", ""))
        attributes[ATTR_STUDY_DATE] = str(getattr(ds, "StudyDate", ""))
findings.explanation: Identifying DICOM fields are copied into MRML node attributes and displayed (DMSAAI.py:770-783), so they persist in any saved .mrb scene/volumes created from these nodes. Nothing leaves the machine, but users saving scenes should know the identity is embedded.
findings.suggestion: Mention in the README that patient identifiers are stored in node attributes and end up in saved scenes, or make the attributes optional.
